explanation: The query returned 12 rows, showing the monthly revenue and cumulative revenue for each calendar month of 2025. The revenue is calculated as the sum of quantity times unit price for completed orders placed in each month. The cumulative revenue accumulates the total revenue from January 2025 through each month listed.

The query returned 5 rows. These rows show the customer IDs, the IDs of the first orders that caused their cumulative spend to reach or exceed 50,000, and their cumulative spend right after those orders.

The query returned 6 rows, showing the percentage of completed orders that were followed by another completed order from the same customer within 30 days for each country. Germany (DE) had the highest percentage at 95.8%, followed by Singapore (SG) at 93.5%, India (IN) at 90.3%, the United Kingdom (GB) at 86.3%, the United States (US) at 84.9%, and Australia (AU) at 80.3%.

The query returned 10 rows, ranking the products by total units sold on completed orders. Products with equal units share the same rank, and the next rank is skipped. The top 10 products by units sold are ranked 1st to 10th, with product IDs 24, 40, 3, 22, 45, 15, 33, 28, 8, and 11.

The query returned 18 rows, listing the top 3 ranked customers by revenue in each country. Customers are ranked using dense ranking, with the highest revenue getting rank 1, and subsequent customers sharing the same rank without skipping the next number. The countries represented are DE (Germany), AU (Australia), SG (Singapore), GB (United Kingdom), IN (India), and US (United States).

The query returned 33 rows, ranking products by units sold in calendar years 2024 and 2025. Products are ranked based on total units sold, with the highest units first. Products with equal units share the same rank, and the next rank is skipped. Only products ranked in both years and with a 2025 rank at least 10 places better than their 2024 rank are shown.

The query returned 48 rows, listing the product category, product ID, and the highest revenue for each product within its category. The revenue is calculated as the sum of quantity times unit price for completed orders. If two products in the same category have the same revenue, the product with the lower product ID is listed first.

The query returned 5 rows, listing the five customers with the highest total revenue and their three largest completed orders. The customer with the highest total revenue is customer 169, followed by customer 253, and so on.

The query returned 9 rows, listing the employee IDs of all employees who report to employee 2, either directly or through other managers, excluding employee 2 themselves. The employee IDs are 6, 10, 14, 26, 30, 34, 16, 20, and 24.

The query returned 20 rows, each showing an employee ID of an Analyst and a NULL value for the top VP ID. This indicates that for each Analyst, there is no direct VP in the reporting chain under the CEO.

The query returned 30 rows, listing the employee IDs of VPs, their direct and indirect subordinates, and the earliest hire dates of those subordinates. For each VP, the subordinate with the earliest hire date and the lowest employee ID is shown.

The query returned 6 rows, showing the number of completed orders placed each day from 1 March 2024 to 14 March 2024. The days with orders are 2 March, 3 March, 7 March, 9 March, 10 March, and 12 March, with each day having exactly one completed order. For the other days in the specified range, there were no completed orders.

The query returned 24 rows, listing every date in February 2024 on which no completed order was placed, in date order. The dates are from February 1st to February 29th, excluding February 14th and February 19th, which had completed orders.

The query returned 61 rows, showing the date and a seven-day trailing average of daily revenue for each day in May 2026. The averages are rounded to two decimal places. The data starts from April 1, 2026, and includes the first 50 days of May.
The query returned 1 row. The customer with ID 265 has a run of 5 consecutive calendar months in which they placed at least one completed order, starting in 2024-05 and ending in 2024-09.

The query returned 10 rows, showing the top 10 customers with the most sessions under the 15-minute rule. Customers 109, 202, and 399 had the most sessions, each with 36 sessions.

The query returned 6 rows, showing the number of completed orders for each country, split by customer segment. The columns represent the country code and the counts for consumer, SMB, and enterprise customers. For example, in the United States (US), there were 465 completed orders for consumer customers, 112 for SMB customers, and 32 for enterprise customers.

The query returned 12 rows, showing the revenue for each month of 2025 by product category. The revenue is calculated as the sum of quantity times unit price for completed orders, categorized by product type.

The query returned 3 rows, showing the total number of orders, the number of cancelled orders, and the cancellation rate for each customer segment. The consumer segment had the highest number of orders (1961) with a cancellation rate of 10.2%. The enterprise segment had 276 orders with a 11.6% cancellation rate, and the SMB segment had 763 orders with a 11.9% cancellation rate.

The query returned 8 rows, showing the revenue from completed orders, the value of returned orders, and the return rate for each product category. The return rate is calculated as the percentage of returned value relative to the sum of completed revenue and returned value, rounded to two decimal places.

The query returned 6 rows, showing the number of one-time, repeat, and loyal customers by country. For example, in Australia (AU), there are 2 one-time customers, 8 repeat customers, and 9 loyal customers.

The query returned 15 rows, showing the first page viewed by each of the customers from 1 to 15. The first page viewed by each customer is as follows: Customer 13 viewed /search, Customer 12 viewed /support, Customer 8 viewed /support, and so on.

The query returned 8 rows, showing the number of distinct customer-days for each page. The page with the most customer-days is /checkout with 368, followed closely by /support with 362. The page with the fewest customer-days is / with 346.

The query returned 8 rows, showing the third page view for each customer and the number of customers who viewed that page. The most popular third page view was /checkout with 64 customers, followed by /product with 56 customers.
